definition: An individual, group, or organization that may affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision, activity, or outcome of a project.
example: The project manager identified every stakeholder before drafting the communications plan.

definition: The approved version of a work product (scope, schedule, or cost) used as a basis for comparison to actual results.
example: Any change to the cost baseline must go through integrated change control.

definition: Budget or time set aside to handle identified risks (known-unknowns) that may occur during the project.
translation: Dự phòng rủi ro đã biết
example: The contingency reserve covered the schedule slip caused by the identified vendor risk.

definition: The iterative process of increasing the level of detail in a project management plan as more information becomes available.
example: Through progressive elaboration, the rough estimate matured into a detailed schedule.

definition: A leadership style where the leader focuses on the growth and well-being of the team and removes impediments so the team can perform.
example: Practicing servant leadership, the Scrum Master shielded the team from outside interruptions.
